preconditions.description: The input `n` must be an integer.

postconditions.description: If `n` is zero or negative, the function returns an empty string.

postconditions.expression: n > 0 and all(len(line) == 2 * n - 1 for line in return_value.splitlines())
postconditions.description: For positive `n`, every line in the returned string has exactly `2 * n - 1` characters (equal to the longest line).
For positive `n`, the returned string contains exactly `2 * n - 1` lines.

postconditions.expression: n > 0 and all(line == ''.join(str(i) for i in range(1, k + 1)) + ''.join(str(i) for i in range(k - 1, 0, -1)) for k, line in enumerate(return_value.splitlines()[:n], 1))
postconditions.description: For positive `n`, the first `n` lines form an ascending pyramid where the k-th line (1-based) is the concatenation of numbers from 1 to k followed by numbers from k-1 down to 1.

postconditions.expression: n > 0 and all(line == ''.join(str(i) for i in range(k, 0, -1)) + ''.join(str(i) for i in range(2, k + 1)) for k, line in enumerate(return_value.splitlines()[n:], 1))
postconditions.description: For positive `n`, the lines after the first `n` form a descending pyramid where the k-th line (1-based) is the concatenation of numbers from k down to 1 followed by numbers from 2 to k.
